$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later. Expected I/O worked out from OpenRGB's C++ (commit d4798c120659ec5ba2e664a9e87bedff8d36f880, Controllers/CorsairPeripheralV2Controller): OpenRGB's own CorsairPeripheralV2Controller, HW/SW controllers, RGBController_CorsairV2HW/SW, CorsairPeripheralV2Devices and KeyboardLayoutManager compiled (g++) with stub headers for hidapi, the logger and threads, constructed and driven against a scripted device ('device': what it answers) by a harness in the porting session's scratch space (openrgb-work/batch2/corsair-v2/driver.cpp, gen.py; not part of the repository). plugin.js was never run to make them. The scripted device answers every request except block-write continuation packets (0x07) with [write_cmd, command, status, value LE (4 bytes)] (hidapi bytes, without the report id); GET 0x12 answers pid_wired for write_cmd 0x08/0x80 and pid_wireless for 0x09 (after wireless_zero_answers zero answers), GET 0x11 0x1B1C, GET 0x41 layout_code, START_TX start_tx_status. 'answers': false = a device that never answers. ops: write = output report (hid_write), read = input report read (hid_read_timeout, len and timeout as the C++ passes them), pause = sleep; hex is the whole buffer, report id first. Two deliberate HueDeck deviations are applied to the C++ output: the VID query (GET 0x11), whose buffer OpenRGB never clears, is sent with zeros in byte 0 and 4..64; and for a product OpenRGB does not know, I/O stops after the product id query. 'leds' / 'size' are the HueDeck grid generated from the same run (devices.js); colours_a / colours_b are per LED in OpenRGB's LED order.
